paper_title: Heteroatom-Bridged Benzothiazolyls for Organic Solar Cells: A Theoretical Study

knowledge_points.content: The heteroatom-bridging strategy involves covalently fastening outer electron-rich thiophene moieties to a central electron-deficient benzothiadiazole (BT) unit using bridging atoms such as C, Si, N, O, or S to enhance molecular rigidity.
knowledge_points.evidence: These heteroatom-bridged DTBTs, whose outer electron-rich thiophene moieties are covalently fastened to the central electron-deficient benzothiadiazole with additional heteroatom bridges, exhibit promising features for OPV applications with rigid molecular structures.

knowledge_points.content: Silicon-bridging in DTBT derivatives induces a specific σ*-π* conjugation interaction between the Si atom and the π-conjugated framework, which effectively lowers the LUMO level and the optical bandgap.
knowledge_points.evidence: The lowest LUMOs and Eg were found in Si-bridged DTBTs, which was proposed to be due to the particular orbital interactions (σ*-π* conjugation) between the Si and the π-conjugated framework.

knowledge_points.content: For a donor material to facilitate efficient exciton splitting and charge dissociation with a PC61BM acceptor (LUMO of -4.2 eV), it should ideally possess a LUMO level near -3.9 eV to maintain a minimum energy difference of 0.3 eV.
knowledge_points.evidence: When the widely used [6,6]-phenyl-C61-butyric acid methyl ester (PC61BM) with a LUMO level of -4.2 eV is adopted as the acceptor, the lowest possible LUMO level of the donor would be near -3.9 eV to offer a minimum energy difference of ~0.3 eV.

knowledge_points.content: The intramolecular rotation angle (θ) between thiophene and benzothiazole in the DTBT framework is highly sensitive; while the rotation barrier is low (< 0.25 eV), rotation can cause significant HOMO and bandgap variations of up to 0.41 eV.
knowledge_points.evidence: A small rotation barrier (< 0.25 eV) was estimated... relatively larger changes of HOMO and Eg up to 0.41 eV can be resulted in by the facile intramolecular rotation.

knowledge_points.content: Heteroatom-bridged DTBT derivatives are classified into two interaction types: Type A (O- and S-bridged) which increases LUMO and decreases HOMO, and Type C (C- and N-bridged) which increases both LUMO and HOMO compared to the parent DTBT.
knowledge_points.evidence: The O- and S-bridged DTBTs are classified as type A (Scheme 1) with increased LUMO but decreased HOMO in comparison with DTBT, while the C- and N-bridged DTBTs belong to type C with typically both increased LUMO and HOMO.

knowledge_points.content: An ideal organic photovoltaic donor material target for 10% PCE (using PC61BM) consists of an optimal bandgap of 1.5 eV, a HOMO level of approximately -5.4 eV, and a fill factor of 0.65.
knowledge_points.evidence: If one assumes an external quantum efficiency of 65% an optimal bandgap of 1.5 eV, and a HOMO level around -5.4 eV of an ideal donor, its PC61BM based BHJ solar cell can achieve a PCE of 10% with a FF of 0.65.

knowledge_points.content: Electronic properties of infinite-length conjugated polymers are theoretically predicted by plotting the HOMO, LUMO, and bandgap of oligomers (monomer to pentamer) against the reciprocal chain length (1/n) and extrapolating to n = ∞.
knowledge_points.evidence: The HOMO, LUMO, and Eg of the polymers were achieved by plotting the HOMO, LUMO, and Eg of the corresponding monomers, dimers, trimers, tetramers, and pentamers against their reciprocal chain length and extrapolating to infinite chain length.

knowledge_points.content: Hole reorganization energy (λh) serves as a qualitative indicator for charge-transporting rates, where lower values correspond to higher rates; for example, TTCBT shows a calculated λh of 0.27 eV.
knowledge_points.evidence: According to eq 1, reorganization energies (λ) can provide a qualitative indication of the charge-transporting rates (the lower the λ values, the higher the charge-transporting rate)... TTCBT [λh] 0.27 [eV].

knowledge_points.content: The calculated absorption peak for the pentamer (CzTTCBCTT)5 at 902 nm is expected to correspond to an experimental polymer absorption peak of approximately 802 nm, based on the observed 100 nm overestimation by the TD-DFT method used.
knowledge_points.evidence: The absorption peak of (CzDTBT)5 around 670 nm is red-shifted about 100 nm compared to the experimental observation... the predicted absorption peak of (CzTTCBCTT)5 at 902 nm can be expected to be actually at 802 nm.

knowledge_points.content: Air stability of the designed heteroatom-bridged DTBT building blocks is inferred from calculated ionization potentials (IP) and electron affinities (EA) that are comparable to known stable materials like DTBT and TNBNT.
knowledge_points.evidence: Since both DTBT and TNBNT were experimentally found to be stable in air, all the designed heteroatom-bridged DTBTs with higher IP and lower EA should have high stability for material synthesis and device operation.
